messages:
Marie Gomez: Quick heads-up — Kestrel SI ran into a blocker on their private deployment. They hit a stop on marketplace image signing and need port whitelisting validated before go-live. Can we do a quick arch review? 11:30 PT works for me. @Omar do you have cycles? :clock11:
Omar Patel: I can jump in. Do we have the exact ports + image signing error logs?
Marie Gomez: Customer sent this error from marketplace during image pull: 'signature verification failed: no valid signatures found' — they use our signed images but are behind a strict proxy. Also asked for the minimum egress ports.
Sahil Rao: For signed images we require TLS to the registry and the signing key check — proxy needs to allow outbound to our signing endpoint. Ports are minimal: 443 and 50051 for the control plane.
Pete Huang: Also there's a collector sidecar that needs 9100 for node metrics, and the healthcheck probes hit 8080 internally. But externally, only 443 and 50051 should be mandatory.
Alice Kim: FYI the marketplace image signing uses quay + our signing webhook at registry.redwood.ai:443 and optionally keyserver.redwood.ai:443. If their proxy blocks SNI we'll need SNI passthrough.
Omar Patel: Can you paste the firewall snippet they asked for? I can validate against our docs.
Marie Gomez: They asked for a minimal whitelist config, here's what I drafted for them:
```
allow_outbound:
  - host: registry.redwood.ai
    ports: [443]
  - host: signing.keyserver.redwood.ai
    ports: [443]
  - host: control.redwood.ai
    ports: [50051]
```
They want to confirm 22 is NOT required.
Sahil Rao: 22 is not required for runtime; only needed if they want SSH into the nodes (we don't require it). Good to call out explicitly.
Pete Huang: Two operational notes: 1) If the proxy performs TLS termination we need their cert chain for image pulls. 2) If they use egress NAT per node, the signing service must see consistent IPs for rate limits.
Marie Gomez: @Omar can you confirm whether our signing service accepts pulls via HTTP proxy with TLS pass-through? Customer currently has an inline proxy that terminates TLS.
Omar Patel: Short answer: not supported. The signing handshake includes client cert validation. If their proxy terminates TLS it will break the signature verification. They'll need passthrough or a proxy that preserves end-to-end TLS (CONNECT).
Alice Kim: We should share the troubleshooting snippet too. If they see 'no valid signatures found' ask them to run:
```
curl -v https://registry.redwood.ai/v2/_catalog \n# and check TLS handshake passthrough
```
Also check image manifest acceptance with `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood.ai/repo/image:tag`
Omar Patel: I'll join the 11:30 PT call and run through their network diagram. Can we get their proxy vendor + proxy config exported before the call?
Marie Gomez: I've requested the proxy config, they'll send by EOD. For the meeting, goal is to unblock the SI so they can complete the field eng runbook. Action items: Omar -> validate proxy passthrough, Sahil -> confirm minimal ports and signing endpoints in a short note, Pete -> add operational caveats to the runbook, Alice -> attach troubleshooting commands.
Sahil Rao: I'll post the short note in this thread after lunch.
deploy-bot: Reminder: scheduled call created — 'Kestrel SI network & image-signing review' 2026-03-22 11:30 PT (video link attached). :calendar:
Marie Gomez: Perfect, thanks everyone. If we can resolve the TLS passthrough bit quickly we can avoid a marketplace rollback. :thumbsup:
Omar Patel: On it.
Alice Kim: I'll prep a one-pager for the SI with the commands and known gotchas.
Pete Huang: I'll update the runbook and mark the SSH requirement as optional.
Marie Gomez: Closing the loop after the call — please post notes here. Thanks!
